answer: A stake-bonded identity check stops Sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a refundable deposit in a vault before it can act, much like a comet that only counts once it has paid the cost of entry. The bond unlocks slowly after sustained honest participation, so one operator running many fake accounts must fund each identity separately, spreading capital across a whole mesa of accounts instead of cloning one free identity. If an account is caught duplicating, colluding, or voting twice, its bond is slashed, turning cheap account farming into a direct, repeated financial loss.
